title: fix(xtask): the batch gate runs its suites in parallel lanes
body:
Stacked on #2779 (merge #2779 first)

Process change: yes

## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate batch` builds each crate alone first. There is one `debug build: <crate> (--no-run)` step for each crate.
- The batch tier then runs its suite steps in the parallel lanes that the release tier uses (`xtask/src/queue.rs`).
- A quick gate that falls back to the batch plan uses the lanes too.
- The batch queue takes its order from the newest `timings.tsv` of a `batch-*` or `release-*` run. The release queue reads `release-*` runs only, as before.
- The `heavy` tier of #2779 and a quick plan stay one step at a time.
- `AGENTS.md` (batch row of the tier table) and the `gate` skill describe the new batch tier.

The gate keeps its guarantees. Each step runs and has its own log. A red step fails the gate. A failed build stops the run. The checkout is read before each step (VOID). The builds, the `ISOLATED` targets, each ui step and clippy run alone with the whole job budget.

## Cause

- `Run::plan` used the lane queue only when the label was `release`. The batch tier ran each step after the other.
- `plan::batch` had one `--no-run` build for all the crates. `crates/kernel` has a dev-dependency on itself with the `truck` feature. The one build gave the shared dependencies the features of all the crates. A later step with one `-p <crate>` resolved a smaller feature set, and cargo compiled that crate again.

## Tests

Pins (all in `xtask`, red before the fix):

- `step_tests::batch_prebuilds_each_crate_without_mixing_feature_sets`
- `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep`
- `lanes_tests::batch_executor_overlaps_lanes_runs_isolated_alone_and_writes_timings`
- `lanes_tests::batch_history_reads_newest_batch_or_falls_back_to_release`
- `tests::batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` (updated: it pins the first batch step)

Mutation results:

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `xtask/src/plan.rs` from #2779 (one build for all the crates) | the two `batch_prebuild*` tests and `batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` | red; green after the restore |
| `Run::new`: `lanes` on for `release` only | `batch_executor_overlaps_lanes_runs_isolated_alone_and_writes_timings` | red; green after the restore |
| `lanes::history_for`: `batch` reads `release-*` only | `batch_history_reads_newest_batch_or_falls_back_to_release` | red; green after the restore |

Gate on head `1da2bcca2`:

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 213 tests pass (191 unit, 22 integration).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (1 step, `xtask unit tests`).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run`: 929 steps. 9 builds run alone, 871 steps are in the queue, 49 steps run alone.

## Wall time

MEASUREMENTS

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes.

## Not exercised

- A 16-core machine. The measurement machine has 8 cores.
- Windows and macOS.
- The post-merge runner (`post-merge.yml`).
- The release tier. Its one debug build for all the crates has the same feature mismatch. This PR does not change the cut gate.

- #2779 (`merge-ready`): the `USAGE` text in `xtask/src/main.rs`. The two PRs change adjacent lines, so this branch has a merge of the head of #2779 (`2b40a8435`). #2779 also changes `plan::heavy_steps` in `xtask/src/plan.rs`. That is a different function.

title: fix(gate): add the light tier for the heavy tests
body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate light` is a new gate tier. It runs the light twins of the heavy tests in release.
- The plan is one release build of the crates that hold a twin. Then it has one step for each test target with a twin (`motion light: lib`).
- A light twin is found from the source. Its ignore reason starts with `light lane:`. Its name is `<full test>_light`.
- The planner refuses a twin by name when its file has no `#[ignore]`d full test. A twin cannot take the place of its full test.
- The first twin is `the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/tests.rs`. It plans the slot 2 times. The full sweep keeps its 20 rows and does not change.
- A red light run prints a note for the PR. The note names each red step and the command of its full heavy step: `cargo xtask gate release --only "motion heavy: lib"`.
- AGENTS.md has two new named rules: **The light lane** ("Testing") and **Local full rerun** ("Commits and Releases").
- `docs/decisions/2569-light-heavy-tier.md` records the choices.

## Cause

- A heavy test was skipped for each patch or run in full at the cut. There was no tier between the two.
- A red heavy test stayed unseen until the cut gate. A red cut gate costs about 53 minutes.

## Tests

Pins, all in `xtask/src/light_tests.rs`:

- `gate_light_is_a_tier_of_its_own`
- `light_plan_is_one_release_build_then_one_step_for_each_target_with_a_twin`
- `the_slot_sweep_keeps_its_full_test_and_has_a_light_twin`
- `a_light_twin_needs_its_name_and_its_full_test_next_to_it`
- `a_red_light_run_names_the_full_heavy_rerun_of_each_red_step`
- `the_law_names_the_light_lane_and_the_local_full_rerun`

Red before the change: yes. On unchanged code the pins do not compile (`unresolved import crate::light`). This is a new tier, thus there is no earlier behaviour to fail an assert.

Mutations:

- The refusal of a twin without its full test was removed: `a_light_twin_needs_its_name_and_its_full_test_next_to_it` was red. Restored: green.
- The `light` tier was removed from `parse_gate`: `gate_light_is_a_tier_of_its_own` was red. Restored: green.
- The `light:` to `heavy:` mapping of the note was removed: `a_red_light_run_names_the_full_heavy_rerun_of_each_red_step` was red. Restored: green.
- A false assert was added to the twin: `cargo xtask gate light` was red (exit code 1) and printed the note with `cargo xtask gate release --only "motion heavy: lib"`. Restored: green.

Readings of the real run (`cargo xtask gate light`, Linux, 6 jobs):

- First release build of `camcraft-motion`: 412 s. A warm build after one test edit: 49 s.
- `motion light: lib`: 18 s. It ran 1 test, and the test passed.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, in two runs. The plan has 9 steps.
  - Run 1 passed steps 1 to 6: `motion build`, `motion suites: lib` (451 passed, 790 s), `adaptive_band`, `adaptive_hsm`, `adaptive_orbit_seam`, `pocket3d_hsm`. The harness stopped the run at its time limit during step 7. No step was red.
  - Run 2 passed the other 3 steps with `--only`: `motion suites: rest_adaptive` (243 s), `motion suites: shape_masks`, `xtask unit tests` (112 s).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The full heavy sweep (`the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations`) was not run. This PR does not change it.
- `cargo xtask gate release` was not run. Its heavy steps run each ignored test, thus they run the twin too (about 18 s more).
- No run on Windows or macOS.
- The light tier is not wired into `/review-prs`, `/merge-ready` or `pr-test.yml`. Issue #2568 owns when the heavy tests of a PR run.

## Owed: the skill text

The issue asks that the cut skill names the local full rerun step. This PR does not change `.claude/skills/`. None. No open PR changes `xtask/src/`, `AGENTS.md` or `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/tests.rs`. PR #2643 and PR #2606 change other files in `xtask/tests/`.

title: fix(post): a flipped Z refusal names the exact reason
body:
## What changed

- A flipped WCS Z does not post. That does not change.
- The refusal now names the exact reason. The issue permits this result: "or the refusal names the exact reason and the decision is recorded".
- The post engine (`post::wcs_flip::apply`) and the verification gate (`app::setup_wcs_flip::setup_problem`) read the reason from one constant, `post::wcs_flip::Z_REASON`.
- The post engine adds a second clause only for a section that has a canned cycle.
- `docs/decisions/2474-wcs-flip-z-refusal.md` records the decision and answers the two open questions of the issue.

The new text of the post engine:

`operation Probe: the WCS has its Z axis flipped; posting a flipped Z is not supported yet - on a control that reads Z reversed, the tool-length word depends on how the tool lengths were measured (a preset length needs G44, a length touched off on that control needs G43), the project does not state which, and the wrong word moves the tool by twice its length; the section also has a canned cycle, whose R plane a mirrored Z puts on the far side of the hole bottom - clear Flip Z on the WCS page`

## Cause

- The old text gave a general reason: "tool-length compensation (G43) and the canned cycles' retract assume the controller's +Z leaves the work".
- The exact reason is this. The tool is on the physical "up" side of its tip. On a control that reads Z reversed, "up" is the control's -Z.
- A register with a preset length then needs G44. A register with a length touched off on that control needs G43.
- The project states only "Z is flipped". It does not state how the tool lengths were measured.
- The wrong word moves the tool by twice its length. The post cannot select the word, so it refuses.

## The maintainer decides

- This PR does not carry a flipped Z into the program. It closes the issue by the second "Done means" clause.
- A carry needs one new statement from the user: how the tool lengths of the flipped setup are measured. The decision file lists what that work includes.
- If the maintainer wants the carry, the issue stays open or a new issue has that work. This PR files no new issue.

## Tests

Pins:

- `a_flipped_z_refuses_by_name` (`crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`, extended).
- `a_flipped_z_without_a_cycle_names_the_tool_length_word_only` (`crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`, new).
- `a_flipped_z_refuses_the_post_by_name` (`crates/app/tests/wcs_flip_post.rs`, extended).

Red before the fix:

- The two post pins failed on unchanged code. The failure showed the old text.
- The app pin failed with the old `setup_wcs_flip.rs`. The failure showed the old text.

Mutations:

- Old `crates/post/src/post/wcs_flip.rs`: the two post pins are red. Restored: green.
- Old `crates/app/src/setup_wcs_flip.rs`: the app pin is red. Restored: green.
- The cycle clause printed for each section (`if true`): `a_flipped_z_without_a_cycle_names_the_tool_length_word_only` is red. Restored: green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 8 steps, 0 failed (post lib, `wcs_flip`, `wcs_flip_dialects`, app lib, app `wcs_flip`, app `wcs_flip_post`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` and an empty `RUSTC_WRAPPER`. The sccache server of the build machine did not answer, and each build stopped after some crates.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. No posted program changes: the change is in refusal text only.

## Not exercised

- The `camcraft-ui` tests did not run. The UI code does not change. Its tests assert the words "a flipped Z is not carried", and the new text keeps them.
- The statement about which dialects have G44 is from general machining knowledge. It was not checked against each control manual. The refusal text does not depend on it.
- The machine door (`machine::untranslated_inversion`, an inverted machine Z) keeps its old text. It is not in the scope of this issue.

## Overlaps

- #2714 touches the same file `crates/app/src/setup_wcs_flip.rs`, in a different function (`op_problem`). Whichever merges second refreshes.

Effort: max

Changelog: The refusal of a flipped WCS Z now names the exact reason: the post cannot know the tool-length word (G43 or G44) on a control that reads Z reversed.

Fixes #2474

title: fix(gate): run the heavy lanes that a diff reaches (gate heavy)
body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate heavy [--base main]` is a new gate tier. It maps the diff to the release `--ignored` heavy lanes that the diff reaches. It runs only those lanes.
- The reach follows the dependencies between our crates. The planner reads them from `crates/*/Cargo.toml`. A source change in `motion` reaches the heavy lanes of `motion` and `app`.
- A changed suite file reaches its own heavy binary only. Shared test code reaches the heavy lanes of its crate. A workspace manifest change reaches each heavy lane.
- A post script, machine file, catalog case or fixture reaches the heavy binaries that read it. The planner uses the mappers of the quick tier for this.
- The steps are the heavy steps of the release tier, with the same names and commands. `--only`, `--failed` and `--dry-run` work.

title: fix(geometry): bridge a fill hole to a walk vertex before a ray hit
body:
## Cause

After #2760 the fig8 mesh is finer. The 2D Adaptive Outside region of the biggest fig8 patch has a hole whose rightmost vertex looks onto a steep, short outer edge. `merge_hole` in `Region::triangles` bridged the hole to the computed ray hit on that edge. The hit point rounds to a point 3e-16 inside the material. The ear clipper then reads it as strictly inside the ears beside it and stops with "no ear in a non-triangle walk". Thus `boundary_viz::preview_fill` gave `None`, and the four frame-cost tests failed. The product code was wrong, not the test helper.

## What changed

- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (`merge_hole`): the bridge candidates are now the walk vertices first, nearest first. The computed ray hits are the last resort. The same checks (no proper crossing, on material) accept or refuse each bridge. A bridge to an existing vertex adds no new point.
- `crates/geometry/tests/geo2d.rs`: new pin `region_triangles_bridge_a_hole_to_a_steep_edge`. `check_triangles` gets an offset form, `check_triangles_in`.
- `docs/decisions/2762-hole-bridge-vertex-first.md`: the decision entry.

#2760 is not reverted. No gouge or containment check changed.

## Readings

- fig8 Outside region: before the fix, no triangulation. After the fix, 1990 triangles. Their area is 6225.768562612561 and the region area is 6225.76856261258.
- The None and Inside regions keep their area.
- The new geometry test fails on the old code: the fill area is 1814.03 against 2223.39, with no error. That is a silent loss of area.

## Pinning tests (green on this code before the gate)

- `frame_cost_caches::pick_lines_build_once_per_input`
- `frame_cost_caches::pick_chips_group_the_welded_faces_once_and_follow_the_picks`
- `frame_cost_probe::area_preview_fill_is_made_once_per_draft`
- `frame_cost_probe::still_frames_on_fig8_name_their_costs`
- The other frame_cost UI tests (8 in total) are green.
- `region_triangles_bridge_a_hole_to_a_steep_edge` and the geometry `geo2d` suite are green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The code commit is b679bbe56. Head 1902ca054 changes only the decision file.

## Effect on toolpaths

`Region::triangles` is not display-only. `motion::entry::dive_room` takes the centroid of the largest clear triangle as the plunge or helix point. A region with a hole can thus get a different dive point. Each candidate is still checked with `Region::contains` and `boundary_clears`, so a changed point stays inside the room.

How I checked: `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib --test machining2d --test adaptive_hsm --test lead_room` is green on this head (451 + 2 + 4 + 68 passed, 0 failed).

## Gate

The quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) falls back to batch because geometry changed. It is still in progress: 222 steps done, 0 failures, at step 223 of about 900. A PR comment will give the final numbers.

## Not exercised

- The app golden CL and G-code suites (for example `golden_cl`, `regression_models`, `first_part_programs`) are not yet run. They are in the batch plan. If a golden output changes because of a new dive point, the gate shows it.
- The heavy release lanes and the pixel snapshots are not run.
- `geo2d.rs` was over 400 lines before this change (now 766). The split is not part of this fix.

Changelog: fix: the 2D area preview fill and the dive-point triangulation no longer fail or lose area when a hole bridges to a steep, short boundary edge.

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: test(ui): run the diag event-level test in a binary of its own
body:
## What changed

`diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` moves from the `diag` unit tests in the `camcraft-ui` lib to a new test binary, `crates/ui/tests/diag_events.rs`. That binary holds this one test only. The test calls `diag::warn` and `diag::info` directly. The lib keeps `the_macros_take_println_shaped_arguments`, which compiles the two macros. The assertions do not change.

## Cause

`tracing` caches the interest of each callsite for the whole process. The test installs a thread-local subscriber with `with_default`. In the lib binary, other tests on other threads call `diag_info!` through the same callsite. If another thread registers the callsite with the dispatchers that it saw before the new subscriber, and that registration ends after the rebuild of the new subscriber, the cached interest is "never". The INFO line is then lost and the WARN line (another callsite) stays. This agrees with the output in the issue. No other test in the lib installs a subscriber. In a binary of its own, no other thread uses these callsites.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/2595-diag-events-own-binary.md` (the dropped options: `rebuild_interest_cache()`, a shared lock, a global subscriber).

title: fix(import): divide the boundary edges of faces curved two ways finer
body:
## What changed

PR #2731 made the STEP chord report true: the report is the highest kept facet edge times the inside bound of the face kind (#2718). `step_fit::fit` never splits a boundary edge. The kernel held the boundary edges only to the pass tolerance. Thus each model with a cone, sphere or torus face read 1.5 x the tolerance and became reduced fidelity. On `fig8.step`, three `shoulder_adaptive` tests failed (main is red, #2754).

This PR divides each shell edge before the pass by the largest inside bound of its faces:

- `step_fit::edge_divisors`: 1.5 for an edge of a cone, sphere or torus face, 1 for all other edges. A cylinder face then gives the largest divisor of its edges to all of its edges, until no edge changes. A wall meshes rim to rim. Two rims with different points make slanted wall facets, and each slice height then cuts a different chord of the wall.
- `CurveGuard::finer` (`step_division.rs`): the edge polyline divides the pass tolerance by that divisor.
- `step_guard::Guarded::new` sets the divisor for each edge.

The edge is divided one time, in the shell's own polyline. Both faces of the edge get the same points, so the shell stays closed. The 1.5 bound and the #2731 report do not change. No test expectation changes.

## Readings (fig8.step)

| Reading | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| reported chord (`coarse_mm`) | 0.00749264 mm (reduced fidelity) | 0.005 mm (full fidelity) |
| facets | 7822 | 7974 |
| outer outline loop (`slice::project`, 64) | 2520 points | 3314 points |
| `shoulder_adaptive` | 3 failed | 8 passed, 1 ignored |

A trial divisor of 2.0 (1.5 with a margin of 4/3) also gave 0.005 mm. But the fig8 Adaptive2D path then ended with an extra ring at the stock edge after the wall pass. The minimum distance to the part stayed 4.000 mm, so there was no gouge. I dropped that divisor. The exact bound (1.5) keeps the path order. The sensitivity of the path order is filed as #2759.

## Pinning tests

- `step_fidelity::a_model_with_faces_curved_two_ways_reports_full_fidelity` (new; fails on main with 0.00749).
- `geometry::import::step_fit::tests::edge_divisors_hold_two_way_faces_and_match_cylinder_rims` (new unit test).
- `shoulder_adaptive`: `fig8_bottom_face_outside_containment_generates_and_stops_at_face`, `fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`, `outside_containment_air_band_fixture_blocks_post` (green again, expectations not changed).

Run one by one: `shoulder_adaptive`, `step_fidelity`, `step_chord_units`, `step_budget`, `tilted_gouge`, the `geometry::import::step` lib tests. Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 22 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- `tilted_gouge_kinds`: there is no such test target in `camcraft-app`.
- The kernel `step_agreement` and `feature_edge_g1_join` suites (known red on main, #2713): not run, not changed.
- Models with sphere or torus faces from outside the fixtures. Where an edge curve's parameter midpoint and the face's differ, the report can go over the tolerance. It then says reduced fidelity; it is never under-stated.
- No golden toolpath or G-code file changed. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Note

PR #2728 (fork, `needs-rework`, #2713) also changes `step_fit.rs`. This PR does not touch its concern (the flip of a flat cap facet) or `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/2754-step-boundary-split.md`.

Effort: max

title: perf(motion): skip blocked doors in the adaptive routed return
body:
## What changed

The cause of #2736 is a slow path. It is not a loop that does not end.

- `adaptive::route::door` (in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/route.rs`) now refuses a door when the disc at the start point holds stock or wall. It refuses before it reads the leg law. Each leg capsule holds its start disc, so no leg longer than `ZERO_LEG` can pass there. The result is the same as before.
- The other door searches read the candidate cells nearest first and stop at the first legal leg. The old search read all free cells nearer than its best cell, in raster order. The chosen cell is the same: the nearest legal cell, and the lower index on a tie.
- `ZERO_LEG` is now one constant in `route.rs`. `lift_link::leg_ok` uses it.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/2736-adaptive-door-search.md`.

## Readings

These are on the issue's region (the box part, area offset 3, D6, optimal load 0.5).

| Build | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| release, HSM plan | 29.6 s | 9.8 s |
| debug, HSM plan | more than 9 min (issue) | 60.2 s |

- Before the fix, the microlift schedule took 23.7 s of the 29.6 s in release. In the schedule, 13 routed returns took 17 s. The door search took 16 s of that, over 53 routes. All 22 doors that failed had a blocked start disc. Each of them read the leg law on each free cell within 6 mm (grid 0.05 mm, about 58k cells).

body:
## What changed

- Ten mill scripts now declare `axisInversion = true`: `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `sinumerik.cps`, `heidenhain.cps`, `mach4.cps`, `grblhal.cps`, `tormach.cps`, `tinyg.cps`, `carvera.cps` and `linuxcnc.cps`.
- Each of them posts a section with a flipped WCS X or Y (#1649).
- Each of them posts for a machine with an inverted X or Y (#374). The two cases use the same flag.
- Each script writes the section note `WCS X FLIPPED - PROGRAM MIRRORED` in its comment form. A plain section after a flipped section does not repeat the note.
- Each script writes the header note `MACHINE X+ MOVES LEFT - INVERTED AXIS`. Doosan DNM and Mach4 had this note already.
- The refusal hint "(Fanuc, Haas)" is now "(each built-in mill post does)". This is in `post::invert`, `post::wcs_flip`, `app::setup_wcs_flip` and the `set_wcs_flip` MCP tool description.
- `linuxcnc.cps` is not in the list of the issue. It is a mill script, and "Done means" says "each mill script".
- No script has a recorded reason why it cannot. `docs/decisions/2475-wcs-flip-mill-posts.md` has the table for each dialect.

## Cause

Only `fanuc.cps` and `haas.cps` declared `axisInversion = true`. The engine refuses the mirror for a script without the flag. No test had read the mirrored program of the other dialects.

## Tests (pins, mutation results)

New file `crates/post/tests/wcs_flip_dialects.rs`, with the new reader `crates/post/tests/mirror_trace/mod.rs`.

The reader reads a posted program as a controller whose X, Y, or X and Y run reversed. It gives the physical cut runs as dense polylines. The test compares each run with the CAM path at equal fractions of the run length. It compares the physical compensation side. It checks that no rapid ends over an X Y that the CAM path does not visit. The reader stops on a G word that it does not model.

The reader reads these forms:
- I/J/K arcs in G17, G18 and G19, and a helix in the dialects that support it
- Heidenhain planar Cartesian arcs; the reader rejects a Cartesian helix
- R-word arcs (`useRadiusArcs`)
- TinyG half-turn arcs, and the chords of TinyG and Heidenhain
- the Heidenhain `I J` centre block
- G81, the Heidenhain G200 with M99, and a hole as plain moves

Fanuc and Haas are in the same table. They calibrate the reader against the scripts that #374 and #1649 verified.

Pins:
- `a_flipped_wcs_cuts_the_cam_path_in_each_mill_dialect` (12 scripts, flip X, Y, XY, with the converse)
- `an_inverted_machine_axis_cuts_the_cam_path_in_each_mill_dialect` (12 scripts, inverted X, Y, XY, with the converse)
- `radius_word_arcs_follow_the_mirror` (the 7 scripts with `useRadiusArcs`)
- `each_dialect_names_the_flipped_axes_and_the_inverted_axes`
- `a_plain_section_after_a_flipped_one_writes_no_flip_note`
- `probing_on_an_inverted_axis_stays_refused_in_the_new_dialects`
- `flipped_x_goldens_for_the_new_dialects`
- `heidenhain_refuses_cartesian_helices_by_operation_name`
- `heidenhain_reader_rejects_cartesian_helices`

The converse is in the two trace tests. The standard program, read by the reversed controller, must stray. This holds for each script and each case.

Mutations:
- The ten scripts as on `upstream/main`: the 7 pins are red. The trace tests stop with "must post: ... does not declare axisInversion = true". Restored: the 7 pins are green.
- `mach4.cps` without the `wcsFlip = ""` reset at the section end: `a_plain_section_after_a_flipped_one_writes_no_flip_note` is red. Restored: green.

Review-fix mutations:

- Removed the reader guard: `heidenhain_reader_rejects_cartesian_helices` is red. Restored: green.

- `wcs_flip.rs` `a_script_that_is_not_verified_for_a_mirror_refuses_by_name`: it now uses the two lathe scripts and `mazak.cps` with the flag line removed.

## What changed

- `camcraft_post::machine` has a new pure data type, `MachineTree`, and a new reader, `parse_mch_tree` (new file `crates/post/src/machine/tree.rs`).

title: perf(3d): facet grid for the drop-cutter support scan
body:
## What changed

- The support facets of 3D finishing are now a `SupSet` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/grid.rs`). A `SupSet` holds the facets and a uniform XY bucket grid in CSR layout (Ericson, "Real-Time Collision Detection", ch. 7).
- These point scans read only the facets of the cell that holds the query point:
  - `support_at`
  - `support_grad`
  - `ball_clear`
  - `column_clear`
  - `edge::fold_best`
- Each scan keeps its own padded-box reject. Each cell lists its facets in ascending index, one time each. Thus the same f64 code runs on the same facets in the same order, and each answer has the same bits as the full scan.
- The cell map is monotone. A facet whose padded box holds the point is always in the cell of the point.
- The grid falls back to the full scan for a non-finite box, a non-finite query point, an extent that is not finite, more than `u32::MAX` facets, or an extent that no cell size fits. It never guesses a cell.
- `SupSet::full_scan` keeps the old scan as the reference. The GPU filter of #2526 can compare against it.
- Each `&[Sup]` parameter in `finishing3d` is now `&SupSet`. The loops that are not point queries read every facet, as before.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2619-facet-grid.md`.

## Readings

Release build, parallel finishing, a height-field mesh, tool diameter 6, tolerance 0.01. One run each, with a temporary harness that is not committed.

| Facets | Before | After | Output hash (before = after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1800 | 13.161 s | 13.908 s | `a629dd9f259d227d` |
| 7200 | 162.915 s | 161.515 s | `c719175f144437ae` |

The grid gives no measurable gain on this job. The point scans are not the hot path here. The output is the same. A profile must find the hot path before more speed work.

## Pinning tests

Lib unit tests in `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/grid_tests.rs`. The scan functions are `pub(super)`, so a file in `crates/motion/tests/` cannot reach them.

- `grid_scan_matches_full_scan_on_bumps`: tool radius 0.4, 0.5, 1 and 3 against cell 1, 0.37, 5 and the automatic size. Boxes on cell borders, and a tool larger than a cell.
- `grid_scan_matches_full_scan_on_big_and_degenerate_facets`: facets larger than many cells, a steep wall, zero-area facets (one point, a repeated vertex, a collinear facet).
- `grid_candidates_hold_every_facet_whose_box_holds_the_point`: the superset law, the order and no duplicates.
- `non_finite_input_falls_back_to_the_full_scan`: NaN and infinite vertices, non-finite query points, an empty set.

The parity tests compare the bits of `support_at`, `support_grad`, `fold_best`, `plunge_support`, `ball_clear` and `column_clear` between the grid and the full scan. A test mutation (a miss of 2% of a cell at the upper edge) makes two tests fail.

- The release lanes and the large-fixture golden runs (`#[ignore]`).
- Parallel raster lines (the optional item of the issue). Not done.
- The speed on the real part models. The readings come from one synthetic mesh.

title: feat(geometry): conservative bit-packed raster of geo2d regions
body:
## What changed

This PR adds `camcraft_geometry::nesting::raster`, slice 1 of the raster nest (#2525). The module is CPU code only. It has no GPU code, no new crate, no new crate edge and no new external dependency.

- `crates/geometry/src/nesting.rs`: the module root (provenance line).
- `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster.rs`: `RasterGrid`, `BitRaster`, `RasterError`, the limits and the two public functions.
- `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster/scan.rs`: the integer scan conversion.
- `crates/geometry/tests/nesting_raster.rs`: 10 tests.
- `docs/decisions/2612-nesting-raster.md`: the unattended decisions.

Public API:

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_CELL_UNITS: i64; // 1 mm
pub const MAX_CELLS: u64;          // 2^24 (4096 x 4096)
pub const MAX_SIDE: u32;           // 2^16
pub fn cell_units_from_mm(mm: f64) -> Result<i64, RasterError>;
RasterGrid::new(origin_x, origin_y, cell, width, height) -> Result<RasterGrid, RasterError>;
RasterGrid::covering(&Region, cell) -> Result<RasterGrid, RasterError>; // origin on the global lattice
pub fn rasterize_over(&Region, &RasterGrid) -> Result<BitRaster, RasterError>; // parts
pub fn rasterize_free(&Region, &RasterGrid) -> Result<BitRaster, RasterError>; // usable sheet
BitRaster::{grid, words, get, count_ones}
```

How it works:

1. The vertices are quantized with the `geo2d` bridge rule (1 unit = 1 um). After that, each cell decision uses exact `i128` arithmetic with checked multiply and add. No float takes part in a cell decision.
2. Pass "touched": each cell whose closed square touches a closed boundary edge. The x extent of an edge in a row slab is rounded outward, and a value on a cell line touches the two cells.
3. Pass "centre inside": even-odd parity of a +x ray at each cell centre, with the half-open edge rule of `geo2d`. Doubled coordinates keep the centre an integer.
4. Over = touched OR centre inside. Free = centre inside AND NOT touched.

A closed square that meets the region but no edge is fully in the interior, so its centre is inside. Thus "over" contains each point of the region. A square with no edge contact and an inside centre is fully in the interior. Thus a "free" cell is a true free cell. Holes are not free.

Rows are packed in `u32` words (LSB first). Padding bits are zero.

Refusals by name (`RasterError`): `NonPositiveCellSize`, `NonFiniteCellSize`, `GridTooLarge`, `EmptyGrid`, `NonFinite`, `OutOfRange`, `EmptyRegion` (`covering`), `RegionExceedsGrid` (`rasterize_over` refuses a part that does not fit, because a clipped part raster is not an over-approximation). `rasterize_free` clips freely, because a cell outside the region is never free.

No raster value reaches posted output or a verdict. The raster only filters candidates. The exact `geo2d` check decides (#2525).

## Type

`feat(geometry)`: the module is a new public API of `camcraft-geometry` for the later nest slices. No user sees it yet, and there is no caller.

## Readings (debug build, one thread)

- Part: annulus r = 50 mm, hole r = 20 mm (256 + 64 vertices), cell 0.1 mm: 1000 x 1000 cells, 662620 set, 2.3 ms.
- Sheet: 3000 x 1500 mm, cell 1 mm (the default): 3000 x 1500 cells, 4491004 free (= 2998 x 1498), 3.9 ms.

title: feat(2d): Slot Undercut for T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop cutters
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the Slot Undercut operation and the cutters for it.

- **Four cutter kinds** in `camcraft-tools`: `t_slot`, `keyseat`, `dovetail`, `lollipop`. They use the existing tool fields. `diameter` is the head. `flute_len` is the head height. `shank_d` and `shank_len` are the neck. `tip_angle` is the dovetail flank angle. The kind words are additive, so `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. The starter catalog has one cutter of each kind.
- **One generator** in `camcraft-motion` (`machining2d::undercut`). It cuts a straight slot or a circular slot (DXF-style bulge). It changes Z at one XY station only, outside the wall. It feeds in sideways, cuts the centre pass and the radial stepover passes at one depth, feeds out the same way, then lifts. The pass offset comes from the widest point of the cutter profile, not from the tip.
- **One verify law** in `camcraft-sim` (`Mode::Undercut`, `verify/undercut.rs`). A move that changes Z while material is in or over the head is `Warning::UndercutLift`. It blocks the post. A neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a `ShankHit`. The operation layer reads the two again against the stock that the earlier operations left (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`). A neck slot that an earlier Slot operation cut is then air.
- **The true profile in the solid law.** The solid law judges a dovetail as a frustum and a lollipop as a full ball (`Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`). The head top gets the same allowance as the tip, so a head that stands under its roof is contact and not a gouge.
- **The true profile in the field stock simulation** (`Stock::simulate_undercut`, `Stock::with_partial_undercut`, `SdfTool::Dovetail`). The head and the neck are two convex solids. The field keeps their union. Both the stock view and Simulate playback cut the head and neck with it. Notice `cut_twin_work::twin_tool` maps `SdfTool::Dovetail` to `"dovetail"`.
- **The column engines cut nothing for an undercut.** A column has one top for each (x, y). It cannot hold air below material.
- **App**: `OpParams::SlotUndercut` (kind tag 44, appended), the project file mirror (keeping `0.0` `bulge` and `neck_slot` keys in JSON), the stamp digest, heights, the part solid law for a part source, and the kept-parts law for both stock and part sources.
- **MCP**: `add_operation` with kind `Slot Undercut` (key `slot_undercut`) and `add_tool` with the new kind words. `verify` reports the new finding kind `undercut_lift`. `list_operation_types` and `edit_operation` include `bulge` and `neck_slot` when they equal `0.0`.
- **UI**: the four undercut kinds in the tool editor (`tool_undercut_row.rs` seeds valid defaults, `Flank angle (deg)` / `flank angle °` edits `ToolKind::Dovetail`, and `Corner radius` stays hidden for undercut kinds), the Slot Undercut page (`undercut_page.rs`), and five original icons (SVG masters rendered with `cargo xtask icons`).
- **Docs**: a Slot Undercut section in the 2D operations guide, and `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md`.

## UI screenshots

Before/after renders from the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU) on `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`) and this PR branch (images stored on `mkinney/Camcraft` `pr-screenshots` commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`):

|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

There was no cutter kind with a head wider than its neck, and no operation for one. The laws for a plain contour are wrong below a roof. The column model reads a pass as a cleared kerf, so a lift through the roof passes as a retract in its own kerf.

title: fix(machine): judge only the quarter points that an arc sweeps
body:
## What changed

`machine::judge::move_extremes` gives the points that the machine travel check judges for one move.
For an arc, it now gives the two endpoints and only the quarter points that the arc sweeps.
The sweep runs from `from` to `to` in the direction of `arc.ccw`, in the arc's own plane (XY, XZ or YZ).
The mill, lathe, plasma, waterjet and wire checks all read this one function.

The check keeps all four quarter points in two cases:

- The in-plane endpoints are 0.01 mm apart or less. Their NC words can be equal, and a control turns equal endpoints a full circle.
- The sweep reads zero or is not finite.

A four-decimal inch post has a 0.00254 mm step on each axis.
Endpoints less than 0.0036 mm apart can round to the same point on a diagonal.
The 0.01 mm bound includes margin and agrees with `ring_zig::MIN_ARC_CHORD`.

The radius is now the larger of the two endpoint radii. The old code used the radius at `from`.

## Cause

The old function added all four quarter points of the arc's full circle.
A 2D Contour cuts a gentle curve as an arc with a very large radius.
The issue's move 31 has a radius of 22170 mm and a sweep of 0.259 degrees.
The check judged points 22 m away from the tool and refused a legal program on each machine size.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/machine_arc_sweep.rs` (9 tests). It runs `machine::check_ops` on one cached move.

- `a_shallow_arc_of_a_large_radius_inside_the_stroke_passes`
- `the_same_endpoints_the_long_way_round_are_refused_on_their_own_side`
- `an_arc_is_judged_on_the_side_that_it_sweeps`
- `a_vertical_plane_arc_is_judged_on_the_side_that_it_sweeps`

| Remove the zero-sweep guard | red: `an_arc_with_no_sweep_to_read_keeps_all_four_quarter_points` |
| Ignore `arc.ccw` | red: the three side tests |

Review fix clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

(MSG, PROBE: G54 OR G55 XY ROTATION NOT ZERO - NO OFFSET WRITTEN)

- The post cannot read the rotation at post time. Only the program can test it.

The issue said that the defect also applies when the target is the active work offset. I did not confirm that part. The guard also covers it, because the rule is not stated. The decision file says how to relax the guard after a run on a control.

## What changed

- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/native.rs` is new. It holds the shared qualified-extension table. The table is empty. Each native CAD extension that is not in the table is refused by name. This includes IGES and `.prt`.
- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/cadmpeg/` is new. It runs the external `cadmpeg` program and gives the STEP text to the STEP importer.
  - It uses the stated path first. If no path is stated, it searches `PATH`.
  - It requires version `0.6.12` or newer.
  - It runs `cadmpeg check --json <input>`.
  - It runs `cadmpeg convert <input> -o <out> --to step --reject-lossy=export`. It never gives `--allow-errors`.
  - The file path is one argument of the child process. No shell runs.
  - Each run uses a private folder below the temp folder. A `Drop` guard removes the folder.
  - A time limit stops the child. A 16 MiB limit applies to the output that the child prints. `MAX_FILE_BYTES` applies to the STEP file.
- `ImportModel::checked_budget` uses the table. The hardcoded `"iges" | "igs"` arm is removed.
- `ViewPrefs` has the new optional field `cadmpeg_path` (`cadmpegPath` in `camcraft-prefs/1`). The key is written only when it is set. Older files load unchanged.
- The UI keeps a stated `cadmpegPath` when it saves the preferences. No UI control sets the path. That is the work of #1876.
- The module `cadmpeg` is compiled only when the target is not `wasm32`.

No shipped import reaches the runner now, because the table is empty. #1875 adds the formats.

## Cause

This is new work for #1572. It is not a defect fix.

## Deviation from the issue

The issue asks for a `cadmpeg formats --json` probe. cadmpeg 0.6.12 does not have this option. `formats` prints a text table only. The first worker on this issue reported this.

This PR does not parse that table. The exit status of `check` and of `convert` is the capability test. A build that cannot read the format or cannot write STEP fails one of the two commands, and the import is refused with the last error line of cadmpeg. `docs/decisions/1873-cadmpeg-runner.md` records this decision and four others. The maintainer can reject it.

title: fix(model): a linked model's digest is of the bytes the import parsed
body:
A linked model's SHA-256 now comes from the same read of the file that the import parsed. Before, the import read the file, parsed it, then read it again for the digest: a file that changed between the two reads recorded the newer digest over the older mesh, and the change was never imported (#2689, found in the review of #2563).

## What changed

- **One read** (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/sourced.rs`, new, native only): `load_model_open_sourced` returns the graded mesh and the digest of the bytes it parsed.
  - OBJ, STEP and `.sc`: the buffer that is parsed is hashed.
  - STL keeps its streaming parse (M5.3 E: the file never coexists with its triangles). A reader hashes every byte it hands to the parser. The ASCII path rewinds to byte 0 once after the sniff; the rewind starts the hash again. Any other seek is refused, so the digest is always of one pass. Bytes after the last binary facet, if the file grew, go into the same pass.
  - Same size cap and the same verdicts as `load_model_open_within`, which stays for the browser build.
- **`ImportModel::within`** uses it on native builds; the browser build records no link, as before.
- **Kernel SHA-256 in pieces** (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/sha256.rs`): `Sha256::new / update / finish_hex`; `hex_digest` is that over one piece. Re-exported as `camcraft_geometry::solidcraft::Sha256`.
- **The link check** (`model_source::read`) hashes the file in 1 MiB pieces. Before, it read the whole file into memory each time a linked file changed, which for a large STL broke the same memory law.
- `stl.rs`: `parse_stream` and `READ_BUF_BYTES` become `pub(super)` for the new module; no other change (the file is over the line limit, so the new code is in its own file).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2689-one-read-digest.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/sha256.rs` `pieces_hash_as_the_whole`: every split (1, 3, 55, 64, 65, 200 bytes) of lengths around the 55/56/64-byte padding edges gives the one-shot digest. The FIPS 180-4 vectors still pass.
- `crates/app/tests/model_link.rs`:
  - `the_link_digest_is_of_the_one_read_the_import_parsed`: for an ASCII STL (the rewind path), a binary STL, OBJ and STEP, the import's digest and the check's streamed digest are the SHA-256 of the file.
  - `the_link_check_hashes_a_file_larger_than_one_piece_as_a_whole`: a 3 MiB file, read in 1 MiB pieces.
  - The 7 tests of #2463 still pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick` (as a separate user with no credentials): 898 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The race itself is not reproduced by a test: it needs a write landing during a parse. The fix removes the second read by construction; the tests pin that the digest is of the parsed read.
- Windows and Linux: not run. No platform branches.
- The browser build (`wasm32`): `web/build-app-wasm.sh` fails on `main` today, before this PR, in the link check from #2463 (`model_link_watch.rs` takes `std::time::Instant`; E0308 at `state.rs:3130`). With that one-line fix on top (a separate PR), this branch builds for the browser: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` exit 0 (Homebrew clang 23 for wasm32).

Changelog: A file that changes while CamCraft imports it is no longer missed: the linked model's digest is now of the bytes the import read (#2689).

Fixes #2689

title: fix(2d): check each contour tab against every cut of its level
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_clear.rs`. After each ring's tabs are fitted, it reads each tab's line on the ring against every other cut of the tabbed levels. The other cuts are: the other keeps of the same ring, the far part of the two keeps beside the tab, and every other ring.
- A cut nearer than the tool diameter `D` cuts into the tab. The loop is held: its tabbed levels cut nothing. A `tabs:` note names the tab and the distance.
- A cut between `D` and `W + D` away leaves the tab at its width. A `tabs:` note names the tab and the width of the strip beside it. The moves do not change.
- `tab_bridge.rs`: a `tabs:` note when the first tab grows back over a picked start. The note names the pick and the point where the tabbed levels start.
- `contour.rs`: one line. The fits of all rings are made before the level loop.
- No posted move changes for a program that gets no new note.

## Cause

The bridge check compared only the two cuts beside a tab. It read the last `W + D` of one walk and the first `W + D` of the next walk. A later run of the same ring, or a different ring, was not read.

## Shape-mask result (on upstream/main `1ae4d061f`)

Tool 6 mm, tab width 4 mm, outside contour, no leads, 0.1 mm grid.

| Case | Distance between the two cuts | Neck of the tab | Note before |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-turn, 10 mm notch | 4 mm | 0.00 mm | none |
| U-turn, 14 mm notch | 8 mm | 1.89 mm | none |
| Second ring, parts 10 mm apart | 4 mm | 0.00 mm and 0.74 mm | none |
| Second ring, parts 14 mm apart | 8 mm | 1.89 mm | none |

A bridge is narrower than the tab width, so the issue is now `P1`.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs` (new) and `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs`:

- `a_tab_that_a_u_turn_of_its_ring_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`
- `a_tab_that_a_second_ring_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`
- `a_tab_beside_a_narrow_strip_is_named`
- `a_tab_with_room_beside_it_has_no_note`
- `the_meter_reads_the_tab_width_on_a_plain_part`
- `a_tab_that_grows_over_a_picked_start_says_so`
- `every_tabbed_level_keeps_the_tab_width` (three tabbed levels)
- `the_bridge_holds_on_the_true_arcs_to_a_tenth_of_a_micron`

Mutation results:

- Old `contour.rs` (from `upstream/main`): the U-turn pin, the second-ring pin and the strip pin are red. The meter reads necks of 0.0 mm. With the fix they are green.
- `moved_start` returns no note: `a_tab_that_grows_over_a_picked_start_says_so` is red. With the fix it is green.
- `every_tabbed_level_keeps_the_tab_width` and `the_bridge_holds_on_the_true_arcs_to_a_tenth_of_a_micron` add coverage. They are green on unchanged code too.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 160 steps, 0 failed, 41 min. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The tab neck meter is `crates/motion/tests/common/tab_neck.rs`. `shape_mask.rs` has 409 lines, so the meter has its own file.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- `SLACK = 1e-6` did not change. A margin grows each tab window on a straight wall and moves the recorded router example program. The test reads the bridge on the posted arcs in chords of `1e-5` mm, and no bridge is under the tab width by more than `1e-4` mm. The decision file gives the bound. The reviewer can ask for the margin.
- `contour.rs` still calls `lead_held` on the first keep when that keep is not at the pick. The new note says that the start moved. A picked start with tabs permits only no lead or a perpendicular lead.
- The neck meter reads outside contours only. The inside slot and bore tests assert the hold and its note, not a neck.
- The new read uses a disc model of the tool. It can hold a loop where the true neck is still the tab width (an acute V-notch, a tab end near a tight fold). Such a hold is safe: the tabbed levels cut nothing, and a note says so.
- The check is local to the tab. It does not follow a stock strip that becomes narrow away from the tab.
- The build used no compile cache: `sccache rustc -vV` did not return on this machine. The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

## Review fixes

Commit `57756c69a` (owner-account takeover, ordered by the maintainer) fixes the two findings of the review of head `edb566d33`:

- `tab_clear::departed` reads a keep that turns back toward its tab before it is `W + D` away (a shallow notch). With one keep, its leads are read the same way. Pin: `a_tab_that_a_u_turn_in_a_shallow_notch_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`.
- `tab_clear::fit_loops` takes the tabbed levels of each loop from the depth ladder. A ring is read against a tab only when the two rings share a tabbed level. Pin: `a_ring_that_stops_above_the_tabs_does_not_hold_another_loop`.
- Quick gate on the new head: 160 steps, 0 failed. Follow-up: #2734.

Commits `3a0570587`, `97c3a445b` and `96f97f424` (owner-account takeover, ordered by the maintainer) fix the blocker of the second review (comment 7007645147):

- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_kerf.rs`. The two cuts beside a tab are also read against the core of the tab line: the line without its first and last `D / 2` (the parts that the end kerfs remove).
- A cut is skipped only while it stays in the disc of radius `D` about the tab end and goes away from the end. A cut in that disc is read against the core outside the disc. From the point where the cut leaves the disc, or turns back toward the tab end, all of the cut is read against the full core.
- A run along the tab at a constant distance is now read. A distance under `D` holds the loop with a `tabs:` note. A NaN distance holds the loop.
- `departed` stays for the "narrow strip" note. The new read can only add a hold, never a note.
- A bore or a slot that is less than about 2 x the tool diameter wide now keeps its tab-height ring of material uncut, with a `tabs:` note.

New tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs`. Each test asserts that the loop is held with a `tabs:` note and cuts nothing under the tab top, or that each tab keeps the tab width:

- `a_tab_that_ends_on_the_return_run_holds_the_loop` (the review case: `notched_to(10, 15)`, start `(32, 20)`, 1 and 2 tabs)
- `a_tab_that_ends_on_the_notch_floor_or_its_corner_holds_the_loop` (start `(30, 18)` and `(32, 18)`, 1 and 2 tabs)
- `a_tab_beside_a_return_run_with_a_lead_holds_the_loop` (`Lead::Perpendicular { length: 4 }`)
- `a_tab_in_a_v_notch_keeps_its_width_or_holds_the_loop`
- `a_narrow_inside_slot_or_bore_keeps_its_tab_ring` (inside, slot 60 x 7 and bore 10, D = 6)
- `a_tab_near_a_corner_of_a_plain_part_is_not_held` (no false hold: 9 outside and 7 inside picks near one corner, 1 and 2 tabs)

Readings on the old `tab_clear.rs` (probe):

- The three tests on the return run, the floor and corner, and the lead fail. The meter reads a neck of 0.000 mm with no note, for example the tab at (25.45, 16.45) for the review case. This confirms the blocker.
- The slot, bore, V-notch and corner tests pass on the old code too. They guard against a loss and against a false hold. The 60 x 7 slot is held by the note "they fill the whole loop". The V-notch tab keeps 3.83 mm (the tab width to one cell).

title: feat(3d): 3D Adaptive gets a Method choice with a Trochoidal method per level
body:
Stacked on #2149 (merge #2149 first)

## What changed

3D Pocket has a new parameter, **Method**, with the values Spiral and Trochoidal.
The Adaptive strategy reads it. The other strategies do not read it.
The default is Spiral. A Spiral operation cuts the same path and has the same stamp as before.

With Method = Trochoidal, each level of the plain ladder is cleared by trochoidal loops.
The loops are planned by the 2D Adaptive lane planner on the cutter-centre area of that level.
The ladder already makes this area: the footprint less the part above the plane, less the tool radius and the stock to leave.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch_level.rs` (new) plans, posts and checks one level.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/troch.rs` (new) holds the state of one run and the entry point `pocket3d_trochoidal`.
- `ladder` gets a `method` argument and four short hooks.
- `OpParams::Pocket3D` gets the field `method`. The project file writes it as the word `method` (`spiral` or `trochoidal`). A file without the word reads as Spiral.
- The stamp gets one byte only for Adaptive with Trochoidal.
- The Passes tab of 3D Pocket shows a Method row when Strategy is Adaptive.
- MCP: `edit_operation` and `add_operation` accept `"method"` in `params`. No new tool is necessary, because the method is a field of the existing parameters.
- The guide page `operations-3d.md` has one new table row and one new paragraph.

Rules of a trochoidal level:

- Each cutting move stays in the level area. The posted level is checked move by move.
- The posted level is checked against the crossing law: its own moves and all moves before it.
- A bore starts on a plane only if the run proved that plane cleared below the disc of the bore helix. If not, the bore starts one plunge height above the stock top.
- A level that the method cannot cut is cut by the Spiral plan. A note gives the reason and the Z of the level. The refused attempt posts nothing.
- In a trochoidal run, each level enters as a first level does. No level reads the plane above as cleared.
- The rest pass, the offset shells and the rotary wrap keep the plan that they had. Their existing notes say so.

These images show the real 3D Pocket Passes tab under `Strategy = Adaptive` on a 60 x 40 x 20 mm pocket block (`1440 x 960`, software/headless WGPU render).

title: fix(sim): excuse a through hole's exit face in ThreadBore
body:
## What changed

- Added `exit: Option<f64>` to `ThreadBore` in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`.
- Set `exit` to `h.through.then_some(h.floor_z)` in `thread_rims::thread_bores` (`crates/app/src/operation/thread_rims.rs`).
- Added `ThreadBore::at_exit` so `wall_radius` excuses a through hole's exit face on the minor circle band when every vertex satisfies `z <= exit + WALL_BAND` and every minor-circle vertex satisfies `z >= exit - WALL_BAND`.
- Required a present `exit` in `excused` to be finite and at or below `top`.
- Added pinning tests in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/thread_op.rs`, and `crates/app/tests/thread_mill_rim.rs`, and recorded the design decision in `docs/decisions/2655-thread-through-hole-gouge.md`.

## Cause

On a through hole, `machining2d::thread_mill` extends the helix one pitch below `floor_z` so the teeth finish the thread out of the bottom exit.
The cutter spans `floor_z` during the lead-in and helix moves, which meet the bottom face triangles on the hole's minor rim.
`ThreadBore` previously knew only `top` (`entry_z`) and excused horizontal mouth facets only at `z >= top - WALL_BAND`.
Every bottom exit facet therefore returned `None` from `wall_radius`, and the solid law flagged each move with `Warning::Gouge` ("move N cuts past the finish surface").

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `thread_mill_rim::a_detected_through_hole_with_tm0600_verifies_clean_and_posts`: failed before the fix with 21 `Gouge` warnings on lead-in and helix moves; passes after the fix with clean verify, empty verification gate, zero stock-sim gouge cells, and clean Fanuc post.
  - `thread_mill_rim::a_through_hole_into_a_lower_part_still_convicts`: passes after the fix (a lower plate below the exit still convicts).
  - `verify::thread_bore::tests::a_through_hole_exit_face_is_excused_while_blind_and_shelves_are_not`: passes after the fix (tests flat and sloped exits, blind holes, intermediate shelves, lower surfaces, inner steps, major radius limits, and non-finite or inverted `exit`).
  - `operation::thread_op::tests::the_thread_grant_reads_the_threads_own_pitch_and_only_over_a_round_wall`: passes after the fix (verifies `exit` is `None` for blind holes and `Some(floor_z)` for through holes).
- Mutation results:
  - Restoring `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs` and `crates/app/src/operation/thread_rims.rs` from `upstream/main`: `a_detected_through_hole_with_tm0600_verifies_clean_and_posts` failed with 21 `Gouge` warnings; restored -> passed.
  - Removing the minor-circle lower bound (`p.z >= exit - WALL_BAND`) in `ThreadBore::at_exit`: `a_through_hole_exit_face_is_excused_while_blind_and_shelves_are_not` failed (`Some(5.0)` instead of `None` at `z = 9.0`); restored -> passed.

- Gate and clippy:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 307 step(s), 0 failed (24.0 min).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with 0 warnings.

title: fix(post): Sodick wire skims on their own LN condition words
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` now posts a Wire Contour with skim passes. Before, it refused each skimmed contour by name (#617, #538).
  - The rough pass keeps its C word after T91, before the first move.
  - Each skim's C word comes after the previous pass's return to the threading point, before the skim's first move. The wire stays threaded. The section has one T91 and one T90. The pass links stay G01.
  - A note line names each skim and its condition.
  - A skim condition id that is not `C` and three digits is refused by name. The app writes no file.
- New boolean post option `approachCondition` (default off). When it is on, the post writes `C000` before the first approach move (threading point to the contour). The operation's C word follows that move. Skims get no C000.
- With the option off, the output for a contour without skims is byte-identical. The #617 goldens do not change.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: the sodick-wire paragraph describes the skims and the option.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2649-sodick-ln-pass-structure.md`.

## Reproduction

On `main` (370d38df6), a punch with the rough condition C001 and the skims C002 and C903 does not post through the Sodick post. The post refuses with "a condition change between passes (skims) is not supported by this post". So no LN1W / LN2W 2- or 3-pass job can post.

## Sources

- Sodick Inc., "Wire EDM Machine Operation Training, LN1W / LN2W Control" (AQ400L, AQ600L, AD360L; part number 6300015, January 2012), public at fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf. We used behaviour only, and we copied no text and no sample program:
  - the word list: C001 for the first cut, C002 for the second cut, C903 for the third cut;
  - the NC program example: the next pass's C word after the return to the start point, with the wire left threaded;
  - the condition header rows: C000 / H000 are named "Approach".
- The existing #617 source (Sodick 1998 "Wire EDM Machine Operation", Mark 21 / EX21) for all other words.

## Inferred, not stated by the source

- The placement of C000. The manual names the row "Approach" but shows no program line with it. For this reason, the option is off by default and applies only to the first approach move.
- Flushing for skims. The manual's example changes the flushing for the finish passes. The post writes no flushing word for a skim. Follow-up: #2686.

## Readings (new golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch_passes.nc`)

- `T91`, then `C001`, then the rough lead-in `G01 X-20.165 Y0.`.
- After the return `G01 X-30. Y0.`: `(SKIM 1 ...)`, `C002`, then the lead-in `G01 X-20.145 Y0.`.
- After the next return: `(SKIM 2 ...)`, `C903`, then the reversed pass from `G01 X-20.135 Y0.`.
- `T90`, `M02`. There is no `G00` between T91 and T90.
- The skim lead-ins match the wire-iso skims golden (`wire_contour_punch_skims.nc`).

- `sodick_wire_passes::a_rough_cut_and_two_skims_post_each_pass_on_its_own_ln_condition` - ok
- `sodick_wire_passes::the_approach_condition_option_cuts_the_first_approach_on_c000` - ok
- `sodick_wire_passes::a_skim_condition_that_is_not_a_sodick_c_word_is_refused_by_name` - ok
- `sodick_wire_post` (8 tests, the #617 golden unchanged) - ok
- Removed: `sodick_wire_post::skims_are_refused_by_name_never_cut_on_the_rough_condition`. Skims now post, and the new file pins them.

- New: `wire_slug_punch_passes.nc`.
- Changed: none. `wire_slug_punch.nc` and `wire_slug_punch_flushed.nc` stay byte-identical.

title: feat(deburr): picked and excluded edges, minimum edge angle, hole filter
body:
## What changed

The 3D `Deburr` operation has four new controls.

- **Picked edges.** When the source is a selection with edge chains, the operation breaks only the exposed edges on those chains. A whole model, the stock, or a selection with no edge chain keeps the automatic detection.
- **Excluded edges.** `exclude_edges` is a list of edge chains. The exposed edges on these chains stay sharp.
- **Minimum edge angle.** `min_edge_angle_deg` removes each convex crease whose face normals bend less than the value. A new operation gets 40 degrees.
- **Hole filter.** `exclude_holes`, `hole_min_diameter` and `hole_max_diameter` remove the rims of recognized round holes (`drilling::recognize`, `recognize_cross`) whose diameter is in the range.

Where the code is:

- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr_filter.rs` (new): the edge filters and their notes. `finishing3d::deburr_edges` takes the picked and the excluded chains. `deburr` calls it with no chains.
- `crates/app/src/operation/deburr_picks.rs` (new): resolves the picked and the excluded chains from the world.
- `OpParams::Deburr`, `sane.rs`, the seed, the stamp digest, the project DTO: the five new fields.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/deburr_page.rs` (new): the rows on the Deburr Geometry tab, and the button "Exclude the picked edges".

Each skipped group of edges gives a note on the toolpath. A picked chain that names no rim and no convex crease is refused by name: a vertical cone over a concave corner cuts the two faces. An excluded chain that is no longer in the model is refused by name.

## Cause

Before this change, the Deburr kernel rode each rim and each convex crease of the mesh. The operation ignored its picks: a Deburr with a selection source rode every edge of the picked models. There was no angle limit, so the facet seams of a smooth convex surface were ridden as edges.

## Decisions (`docs/decisions/1888-deburr-edge-filters.md`)

- The issue says to remove Deburr from the `!selection_drives_region` guard. I did not do that. That guard makes a 2D area from the picks and refuses an open chain. The picks are read as paths, the same as Multi-Axis Contour drive chains. The result is the behaviour that the issue asks for.
- A project file without `min_edge_angle_deg` reads 0 (every crease). That is the path the file stored. The seed for a new operation is 40. Each new key is absent from the file at its rest value, and the stamp digests a filter only off its rest value. An old automatic or face-only operation keeps its cached path unchanged. A chain-selected operation must regenerate once. Its stamp versions the changed selection behavior.
- The minimum angle and the hole filter apply to the automatic edge set only. A pick is an explicit instruction.
- A face, patch or vertex pick in the source keeps its old meaning: it names the model that the operation reads. `turned_selected_deburr_cuts_like_the_baked_part` (#2284) pins that reading. The first version of this branch refused a face pick, and the quick gate failed on that test. Only an edge chain narrows the ride.
- No new command: the new fields are operation parameters. `EditOperationParams` (UI Apply, MCP `edit_operation`) and `SetOperationGeometry` (MCP `set_operation_geometry`) carry them. No MCP follow-up issue is necessary.

## Tests (pins, mutation results)

Motion, `crates/motion/tests/deburr_filters.rs` (new, 7 tests):

- `a_crease_below_the_minimum_edge_angle_is_skipped_out_loud`
- `a_picked_chain_rides_alone`
- `a_pick_that_names_no_exposed_edge_refuses_by_name`
- `an_excluded_chain_is_left_out_of_the_automatic_edges`
- `a_hole_rim_inside_the_diameter_range_is_skipped`
- `a_cross_hole_rim_inside_the_diameter_range_is_skipped`
- `the_filter_doors_refuse_by_name`

App, `crates/app/tests/deburr_edge_filters.rs` (new, 8 tests):

- `a_picked_edge_is_the_only_edge_broken`
- `a_face_pick_names_the_model_and_keeps_the_automatic_ride`
- `an_excluded_pick_that_is_gone_is_refused_by_name`
- `an_excluded_edge_stays_sharp`
- `the_minimum_edge_angle_reaches_the_kernel`
- `a_hole_inside_the_diameter_range_keeps_its_rim`
- `the_command_door_refuses_a_bad_filter`
- `the_filters_round_trip_the_project_file`

App, `crates/app/tests/mcp_deburr.rs` (new): `deburr_takes_edge_chains_and_its_filters_through_mcp`.

Changed tests: `the_deburr_seed_carries_the_heights_and_a_hand_break_width` asserts the seed values. The UI tab table in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs` names the new Geometry rows. Six test files that build `OpParams::Deburr` by hand got the new fields at their rest values.

title: fix(multiaxis): Rotary Parallel leaves the end face of a held end
body:
## What changed

- Rotary Parallel now reads the setup stock.
- An end of the model is a held end when the stock goes on past it by more than one tool diameter (plus the tolerance). This is a bar that goes on into a chuck or onto a centre.
- At a held end the centre of the ball does not go past the end plane of the model. The end face is not cut. The turned surface is finished to its end.
- The operation adds a note that names the end: `Rotary Parallel: the stock goes on 19.050 mm past the end of the model at (-31.750, 0.000, 0.000) - that end face is left, and the tool stops at its plane`.
- Under the sloped-entry law, a ramp does not start past a held end. That infeed stays a radial plunge.
- A model with no length between two held ends is refused by name.
- A free end is cut as before. Stock that goes on by one tool diameter or less is a facing allowance and is cut as before.
- The #1904 example project and program are generated again. The two guide pages and the two pictures follow the new program. The guide page drops its "air cut only" limit and keeps the air cut as the first run.

New code:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_ends.rs` (new): `held` reads the two ends, `clip` keeps the cutting moves in the window.
- `rotary_parallel_in(facets, stock, params, axis)` in `rotary.rs`. `rotary_parallel` calls it with no stock.
- `rotary_links::Ramp` has the field `span`.
- `generate.rs` passes the stock facets (one line).

## Cause

`rotary_parallel` ran the finishing raster over the whole model and did not know the stock. The pass down the chuck-side end face was a slot one tool diameter wide from the skin of the bar to its axis.

## Tests

Pins:

- `camcraft-app` `continuous_4axis_part::the_pass_leaves_the_chuck_side_end_face` (replaces `the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline`). Red on unchanged code: `the tool passes the chuck-side end plane: X-1.3171`.
- `camcraft-app` `continuous_4axis_part::a_short_flute_posts_now_that_the_chuck_side_end_face_is_left` (replaces `a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`). The shank refusal came from the cut that is gone.
- `camcraft-motion` `rotary::the_parallel_leaves_the_end_face_where_the_stock_goes_on`: held end, free end, sloped entries, facing allowance, flush stock.
- `camcraft-motion` lib `multiaxis::rotary_ends::tests` (3 tests): the window, the refusal, the clip.
- `site/tests/test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py`: 14 tests pass.

The `#[test]` count of `continuous_4axis_part` is the same (9).

Mutation results:

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| The clip is off (`rotary.rs`) | `the_parallel_leaves_the_end_face_where_the_stock_goes_on` | red: `the ball center passed the held end's plane: station -1.014` |
| The clip is off | `the_pass_leaves_the_chuck_side_end_face` | red: `X-1.3171` |
| The clip is off | `a_short_flute_posts_now_that_the_chuck_side_end_face_is_left` | red: `post blocked - 23 warning(s): Journal: shank/holder at move 1380 collides with the uncut stock` |
| The ramp guard is off (`rotary_links.rs`) | `the_parallel_leaves_the_end_face_where_the_stock_goes_on` | red: `a ramp runs in from past the plane` (from station -8.03) |
| `generate.rs` as on main (no stock passed) | `the_pass_leaves_the_chuck_side_end_face` | red: `X-1.3171` |

Each pin is green with the fix restored.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 129 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the final head.

The gate ran before two clippy fixes in `rotary_ends.rs` (a `partial_cmp` in place of a negated comparison, and one doc comment line). After them, these ran green on the final head: the `rotary_ends` lib tests, the `rotary` and `rotary_links` suites, the `continuous_4axis_part` suite and the site page test.

## Goldens moved

One: `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` (3213 lines to 3125 lines). `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` holds the same toolpath as its cache.

- 1306 `G1` lines past the chuck-side plane (X below -1.25) are gone. These are the end-face cut.
- 1210 `G0` lines and 42 `G1` lines are new at the chuck-side end (X-1.25 to X-1.15). These are the retract, the A index on the clearance radius and the plunge of each pass.
- 21 `G1` lines at the chuck-side end are gone: the passes now stop at X-1.25.
- About 12 lines in other places differ. The `G93` or `G94` word is on a different line of the same moves, or an A or F word differs in the last digit.
- The free end is the same: the lowest Z at X above 0 is -0.0322 before and after.
- The project file version goes from 70 to 71. Main moved the format after the example was written.
- No snapshot PNG changed. No other `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

- No machine run and no PathPilot simulator run of the new program.
- A model with a domed or coned held end. The rule keeps the centre of the ball inside the end plane, but the pass still cuts that dome or cone up to the plane.
- A bar with two held ends in the app (the kernel unit test has it).
- A tilted fitted axis with a stock: the test bars lie along X.
- The kit golden `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc` does not change. Its stock ends where its model ends, so CamCraft reads air there. The guide pages now say that the stock must be as long as the bar.

The continuous half of #1904: a step-by-step guide page for the Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, with a committed demo project and drawn pictures.

- **Page:** `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-continuous-4axis-part.md`, "Your first continuous 4-axis program". It covers: how the bar is held; the machine file's four A values (axis, travel, `nose_to_axis`, A rate) and what to compare with the machine; finding the A centreline and setting G54 on it; the ball tool; a Rotary Parallel operation, setting by setting; the checks and what the stock simulation says; the posted program read line by line; what the post refuses; a run in the PathPilot simulator; then a single-block start and an air cut with no bar.
- **What the post writes, in plain words, from the Hub readings on #796:** `G93` on a feed that turns A with X Y Z, and why (reading 2: in `G94` F is the X Y Z distance only; reading 3: `G93` is accepted and timed); the A rate cap worked out on real lines; an A-only feed in `G94` with F in degrees per minute (reading 4); A counting on through 180 (reading 1); `G94` back before the last rapid.
- **Demo project:** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`, the program it posts `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` (3213 lines) and the model `examples/models/first-continuous-4axis-part.obj` (made by `gen_first_continuous_4axis_part_obj.py`). #2342's kit project was not reused: it has no continuous operation, and its wrap golden has a stock that ends where the model ends.

No PNG, no screenshot. The UI renderer of #1902 (PR #2078) is not merged, so there are no UI renders yet.

1. **The page ends with an air cut and tells the reader not to cut.** Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model down to the axis. On a bar held in a chuck, the chuck-side end face is inside the bar: the program feeds to Z-0.03 at X-1.3125 while the stock goes on to X-2. 2. **The shipped machine leaves A travel unstated.** Rotary Offset can count past one turn on this machine file. A custom machine with bounded A travel can refuse that count. Filed as **#2344**.

- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs`: `digest_of` uses a fixed array, not a heap `Vec` for each triangle (the same hash). `patches` and `patch_rings` build the lattice one time.
